subject: POC/Trial next steps (ACME) - environment options & timeline
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Chen <jamie.chen@acme.com>, Alex Li <alex.li@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: POC/Trial next steps (ACME) - environment options & timeline

Hi Jamie / Alex

Thanks again for the time today — really useful conversation. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off the POC smoothly. Please confirm or add anything I missed.

Summary of success criteria you shared:
- Latency: 95th percentile < 150ms on 8k context for the main inference route
- Throughput: sustain 20 concurrent sessions at 10 qps each for peak load tests
- Cost target: ~0.6 tokens/sec/node cost target for evaluation phase (measured by Redwood Optimize)
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and E2E encryption in transit; dedicated audit logs preferred
- Functional: feature parity with current embeddings + chat flow, correct reranking behavior on test set

Proposed evaluation plan & environment options (pick 1 primary):
1) Hosted trial (fastest) — Redwood hosted API, full observability, easiest onboarding. Good for functional and basic perf checks.
2) Dedicated sandbox (recommended for perf validation) — reserved GPU pool in our Dedicated offering to reproduce throughput/latency under load. Requires a short provisioning window (3-5 business days).
3) VPC trial (if required for compliance) — customer-managed VPC deployment; best for strict network controls but adds setup time and procurement (2+ weeks).

Proposed timeline (flexible):
- This week (May 25–29): finalize success criteria and pick environment; schedule SE kickoff
- May 29–Jun 4: hosted trial provisioning OR dedicated sandbox provisioning starting (if chosen)
- Jun 7–Jun 14: performance testing & eval; run benchmark harness and validate metrics
- Jun 15: review results and decide next steps (scale / purchase / dedicated contract)

Ownership & next steps:
- Customer owner: Jamie Chen (confirm test dataset + access)
- Redwood sales: Marissa (point of contact / procurement)
- Redwood SE: Rafael / Monica (technical onboarding + perf testing)

I attached a short POC plan doc (poc-plan-acme.pdf) with the test harness and data checklist.

Can you confirm: 1) which environment you prefer to start with (hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC), 2) target date to start (earliest preferred), and 3) who will provide the test dataset?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Chen <jamie.chen@acme.com>

Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC/Trial next steps (ACME) - environment options & timeline

Hi Marissa—

Thanks for the clear recap. Agree with the success criteria as written. Quick answers to your questions:
1) Preference: start with the Hosted trial to validate functional behavior and iterate quickly. If we see performance gaps, we want to move to a Dedicated sandbox for full load testing.
2) Target start: we'd like to begin the hosted trial the week of June 1, goal to complete perf validation by June 14.
3) Dataset: Alex will provision a subset of our production-ish test dataset (anonymized) by Friday, May 29.

Two asks: can you share SOC2 artifacts and a short security questionnaire? We'll need those for our procurement team. Also, if Dedicated sandbox is needed for perf, we'll need an estimate of provisioning lead time and any cost implications.

Attaching ACME security questionnaire (acme-security-questionnaire.pdf) for your team to fill out.

Thanks—
Jamie
Director of Product
ACME Corp

Marissa / Monica—

I can own the SE kickoff and perf harness. Monica, can you be the technical lead for the Dedicated sandbox provisioning if we need it?

Planned next steps (internal):
- May 28: prep perf harness and baseline on Hosted using a synthetic dataset (Rafael)
- May 29: customer dataset arrives — run quick smoke tests on Hosted (Rafael + Monica)
- May 29–Jun 2: if we see >20% perf degradation versus baseline, provision Dedicated sandbox (Monica to coordinate provisioning and provide cost estimate)
- Jun 3–Jun 10: run full throughput/latency tests in Dedicated sandbox and collect Redwood Optimize metrics

Cost/lead-time note for Marissa: Dedicated sandbox provisioning typically needs 3 business days (once code/config approved) and the approximate incremental cost for a 1-week reserved eval is ~$6k USD for the GPU pool to reproduce the ACME workload. I'll prepare a short estimate doc by EOD May 27.
